title: Meta Taps Chinese Startup Fourier To Build First Humanoid Robot Prototype

tickers.name: Meta Platforms, Inc. Class A Common Stock

summary:
The newly developed robot, known internally as Max, is designed to handle common household chores and serve as a physical manifestation of Meta's Muse AI agent. The 106-pound humanoid prototype was built in three months through a partnership with the Shanghai-based startup Fourier and runs on an Nvidia Jetson Thor chip.

Meta is currently developing a second version of the robot with upgraded sensors for stair navigation and improved hands. While the company is hiring robotics engineers in China to scale its development efforts, it stated the current project is for internal research and the machines will not be sold. The cooperation with Fourier comes as U.S. regulators move to restrict the import of humanoid robots from China.

selectedTweets.text:
Meta built a humanoid robot prototype with China’s Fourier in just three months—but the collaboration comes with geopolitical complications.

The Information’s Jyoti Mann explains:

“Neither government is necessarily thrilled about the broader implications of such a cooperation, but Meta is currently just saying this is an internal research and experimentation project. It doesn't have any plans to sell these particular robots.”

selectedTweets.text:
🚨 BREAKING:

Meta reportedly has built a prototype humanoid robot, in partnership with Chinese startup @FourierRobots.

Fourier is one of China’s most capable humanoid hardware companies, sophisticated bipedal platforms, strong actuator supply chains, deep manufacturing expertise. 

I've met them couple of times, and was really impressed with the robots. Their roots are in exoskeletons + rehab robotics.

The robot is called Max, and here’s what we know about it:

→ Built in approximately three months
→ Weighs around 106 pounds (48 kg)
→ Meta is already building a second version
→ Meta has no plans to sell these units
→ Framed internally as the physical embodiment of Meta’s Muse agent (@alexandr_wang bring it on!), designed for household tasks

For Meta, partnering with a Chinese hardware company to build a prototype is the fastest path to having something physical to work with while its AI and software teams develop the intelligence layer.

This isn’t a manufacturing robot, but rather home robot. Similar move to acquisition of Fauna Robotics by Amazon earlier this year.

Meta is building a physical body for its AI agent, the same way a phone is a physical body for an operating system.

Every major AI lab (Sam Altman also announced that will reveal a humanoid robot in 2027) is arriving at the same conclusion. 

The next frontier is not software on screens. It’s AI in the physical world.

It was first reported by @theinformation (@jyoti_mann1).

selectedTweets.text:
Meta reportedly built a humanoid robot together with the Chinese robotics startup Fourier, according to The Information.

The robot is called @Meta "Max." It weighs about 106 lb, was built in roughly three months and runs on Nvidia's Jetson Thor chip. Work on a second version started in September.

Meta says it's for research only. Still, pairing up with a Chinese hardware maker shows how fast Meta wants to get into robotics, and how much of the humanoid supply chain now sits in China.
